parameters.content:
test details:

chat: i am at 135w 15th street nyc. where can i park my citibike

siri webhook: POST /webhook/citibike-siri
arrival webhook: POST /webhook/citibike-arrival

options.systemMessage:
you are only the request-understanding layer for a citibike assistant.

read the newest user request together with conversation memory and turn it into the structured fields requested by the output parser.

intents:
station = user wants live information about one specific citibike station
place = user wants good return stations near an address, landmark, intersection, school, office, or neighborhood
gps = user gave current latitude/longitude and a destination, or shared gps after already stating a destination
network = user asks a broad question about the citibike system overall
remember = user tells you that a named place/alias like school, home, work, gym, etc maps to a specific usual citibike station
help = you genuinely need clarification or theyre asking what the assistant can do

rules:
- use conversation memory to resolve things like "my school dock" after the user previously told you what school means.
- if the user says "my usual school dock is e 17 st & broadway", intent is remember, alias is school, rememberedStation is e 17 st & broadway.
- if the user later says "check my school dock", intent is station and stationQuery should be the actual remembered station name, not the words "my school dock".
- if the user asks "find somewhere to dock near stern", intent is place and placeQuery should be a clear nyc geocoding query. for obvious shorthand you can expand it, for example stern -> nyu stern school of business, 44 west 4th street, new york.
- if the user gives coordinates plus a destination, intent is gps. put the coordinates in currentLat/currentLon and destination in placeQuery.
- if a gps location message says to use the previous destination, use memory to fill placeQuery. if no destination exists in memory, use help and put a short question in clarification.
- if they ask whether a named station is full, intent is station.
- if they ask about total bikes, full stations, or the network overall, intent is network.
- usualStation is only for a destination/place/gps request when a known usual station is relevant. otherwise use an empty string.
- use empty strings for unused text fields and 0 for unused coordinates.
- do not answer the user here. only classify and extract.
- messages from siri may end with "(my current gps coordinates are LAT, LON)". that is the riders live location, not a request by itself. whenever it is present, copy it into currentLat/currentLon, whatever the intent.
- if they want a dock near me / near here / nearby / around here and coordinates are present, intent is gps and placeQuery is an empty string.
- if they name a destination and coordinates are present, intent is gps and placeQuery is that destination.
- placeQuery is sent to an address geocoder (openstreetmap) that only matches street addresses and official place names, never descriptions. ALWAYS rewrite placeQuery as a plain street address with the borough when you know it, otherwise the official name. examples: "jp morgan headquarters" -> "270 park avenue, manhattan". "the empire state building" -> "350 5th avenue, manhattan". "my gym on 14th and 8th" -> "west 14th street and 8th avenue, manhattan". "barclays center" -> "620 atlantic avenue, brooklyn". never include words like headquarters, office, building, near, or the.

nodes.name: pick a dock near the destination

parameters.content:
general idea: 

The idea for our project came from a pretty simple problem our group kept running into. The two Evans would ride Citi Bikes around campus pretty often, and when we got to where we were going, a lot of the nearby docks would already be full. That made us think about building something that could check live Citi Bike availability, remember the docks we normally use, and quickly redirect us to another nearby station if needed.
So far, we have built an n8n-based chat workflow that can understand normal user prompts, check the live status of a specific Citi Bike station, find nearby stations around a destination such as NYU Stern or Washington Square, compare open dock availability, and recommend an alternative if the usual station is full or not accepting returns. The workflow can also remember things said earlier in the conversation, such as “my school dock is E 17 St & Broadway,” and then use that information later when the user asks something like “check my school dock.” We also added support for GPS coordinates, so if the user provides their current latitude and longitude along with a destination, the workflow can estimate how far away they are and recommend the best station near where they are going. We are currently working on setting up Telegram and voice functionality so the system can accept spoken input and return both text and audio directions. The final step is to connect it to live GPS automatically, so while someone is riding, the system can recognize when they are getting close to their destination, check dock availability ahead of time, and tell them through their headphones whether to continue to their normal station or reroute somewhere else.

ios arrival mode (commuters)

shortcuts POST here: an Arrive automation near school/work/home, or the Action Button.
body: {"place":"school","address":"44 W 4th St","usualDock":"Mercer and Bleecker"}  (or destLat/destLon, or lat/lon for 'near me')
address can be a name ("NYU Stern"). it's looked up in openstreetmap within NYC; if that fails the model turns it into a street address and we try again.
each address is looked up once and remembered (workflow static data). the first answer for a new address says what was found.

siri mode ("hey siri, dock check")

the iphone shortcut asks what you need, then POSTs here:
{"text":"find me a dock near stern","lat":40.73,"lon":-73.99,"sessionId":"evans iphone"}

it runs through the same ai request-understanding as chat, and the answer comes back as one plain sentence that the shortcut speaks over your headphones.
